frames.narration: Checkout v2 is deployed next to v1 on a few instances. It has a latent bug (about 2% failures, v1 has 1%) that staging never showed. It gets no traffic yet.
The splitter sends 5% of the 1000 requests per minute to v2: about 950 to v1 and 50 to v2. Routing by user id keeps each user on one version.
Both versions report errors and latency to the gate. After 5 minutes v2 has served about 250 requests, so the gate keeps baking until it has 300.
At minute 6: v2 has 4 errors in 311 requests (1.3%), v1 has 59 in 5689 (1.0%). The gap is within random noise, so the gate passes and widens to 25%.
At 25%, v2 gets 250 requests per minute. The bug is now visible, but the gate still needs a sample. After 3 minutes: v2 has 15 errors in 762 requests (2.0%).
v1 over the same minutes: 17 errors in 2238 requests (0.8%). v1's rate predicts about 6 errors for v2, and v2 has 15. That is nearly 4 standard deviations above the baseline: not noise.
The gate trips and orders a rollback: v2's weight goes to 0 and v1 carries 100% again. No human was needed.
Cost of the bug: about 19 failed requests out of 9000 served in 9 minutes. A full release would have failed 2% of all checkouts, around 20 every minute, until someone noticed.
